2. The petitioner M.A. Razzaque is the owner of the properly comprising an area of 0.8i acres of land together with .32 acres of land of earth cutting out of .42 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 278, C.S. Khatian No. 150 of mouza Razarbagh by purchase through a registered kabala dated 19.5.53. The petitioner submitted a plan for construction of a building which was approved by the C and B Department and ever since the petitioner is in possession of the same and his name has been recorded in the S.A. record and also in the subsequent records of right. The original C.S. Plot No. 278 comprising an area .42 acres of land was requisitioned for the purpose of acquisition in LA, Case No. 120/60-61 for earth culling for raising the level of the Kamalapur Railway Station. It is staled that no notice was ever served upon the petitioner as to the requisition or acquisition of the properly in question in L.A. Case No. 120/60-61. The petitioner did not know about the aforesaid requisition or acquisition of the property, the petitioner's possession was never taken away or threatened at any stage but subsequently he came to learn that the afore-said house was requisitioned and acquired. It has also been notified on 23.12.91 that person’s concerned were directed to remove their structures which fell in the L.A. Case No. 120/60-61 within 31.12.91. The petitioner in the meantime had already submitted the representation to the authority asking for derequisition or release of the said properly. An inquiry was made into the matter and the inquiry report disclosed that the delivery of possession of the petitioner's property was not taken and further the erstwhile owner one A. Salam took the compensation money but strange enough that the petitioner's name had been published in the records of right since his purchase both the S.A. and R.S. Klialians but no notice was served upon the petitioner. The petitioner filed an application along with attested documents, namely, documents and other papers but his prayer was not allowed and rather by the impugned order dated 6.1.94 his prayer for release or derequisition of the properly has been refused simply on the ground that he may be informed that there is no scope for release or derequisition of the property. 

 3. An affidavit has been filed on behalf of respondent No. 1. As to the purchase of land by registered Kabala and possession of the petitioner the respondent has stated that these facts were not known to them. In respect of the record it is barely staled that the papers were not available to the Collectorate Office. The respondent No. 1 cannot say whether any application for release of We property was at all filed on 9.10.89 or on 22.4.91. It is stated in paragraph 15 of the affidavit that the land so acquired was transferred to the requiring body which was published on 23.12.91 in the Daily Ittefq but the petitioner has clearly asserted that after his purchase of the land by registered Kabala dated 19.5.53, he was in peaceful possession thereof and his plan for construction of the build was duly approved by the authority and he made construction thereon, paid taxes etc. Upto 1994 and his name has also been recorded in the record of right, delivery of possession was not taken over from the petitioner, no notice was served up on him relating to the requisition or acquisition of the property and after his purchase by Kabala dated 19.5.53 he mutated his name which published in the records of right such as S.A. and R.S. Khatians. On the face of such clear assertion of owning and possessing the properly and paying the taxes, rents etc. and his name being published in the records of right the respondent ought to have served notice upon the petitioner as to the requisition on acquisition of the properly. Furthermore in their affidavit-in-opposition respondent No. 1 staled that delivery of possession of the properly has already been given to the requiring authority but the fact remains and also admitted by the respondent that the petitioner has been in peaceful possession of the properly by constructing building thereon. In matters of requisition for the purpose of acquisition notice is mandatory and one's properly cannot be taken away without due notice as such requisition or acquisition so far the petitioner's properly is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction. Furthermore when, the respondents formed an inquiry committee to inquire into the matter and the report was that the petitioner was in possession the respondents ought to have derequisitioned or release the properly at once as the petitioner's land admittedly is an excess land which remains with the Government. At any rule the Government has no right, title or interest in the property as the same is in peaceful possession of the petitioner after purchase. It is asserted that under the provision of East Bengal Emergency Requisition of properly Act, 1948 the Government requires to serve notice upon the occupant or the owner. That having not been done the so-called acquisition and requisition is without jurisdiction.
